questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: What astronauts like to eat and drink in space
How wine is made in the vineyards of France
How growing plants in space could help Earth farming
Why Mars could soon be used for large-scale farming
questions.why: Georgina says they'll find out how growing plants in space can develop better crops on Earth.

questions.q: What was the real purpose of sending wine to the space station?
options: To study making food and drink in space for Earth
To give the astronauts a special treat with dinner
To test whether glass bottles break in low gravity
To advertise a famous French wine company worldwide
questions.why: Neil says the real purpose was to explore producing food and drink in space for people on Earth.

questions.q: What kind of light does Vertical Future use to grow plants?
options: Natural sunlight through windows
Mostly green light
White light of all colours
Only red and blue LED light
questions.why: Jen Bromley says they only use red light and blue light, which is why the room looks pink.

questions.q: Why do the plants look black under these lights, according to Jen Bromley?
options: They are dying from lack of sunlight
They absorb all the light and reflect none
They are a special black variety
The room is kept very dark
questions.why: She says they look black because they're not reflecting any light and use every photon.

questions.q: What did Nasa find about different 'light recipes'?
options: They make plants grow only at night, not in the day
They have no real effect on how the plants grow
They can change a plant's shape, size and flavour
They make plants grow well without any water at all
questions.why: Georgina says different colour combinations can change a plant's shape, size and even flavour.

questions.q: According to Gioia Massa, what is the biggest challenge of growing food in space?
options: The lack of natural light
Microgravity
The cold temperature
The lack of soil
questions.why: Neil says lack of light isn't the biggest obstacle, and Massa says microgravity is really challenging.

questions.q: How are plants able to survive in space?
options: Astronauts give them extra food
They grow very slowly
They are protected in special boxes
They adapt by switching their genes on or off
questions.why: Massa says plants have plasticity: they can turn their genes on or off to adapt.

questions.q: Why might plants from space be useful back on Earth?
options: Being stressed makes them stronger and more resilient
They taste much better than plants grown on Earth
They don't need any light at all to grow back home
They grow much bigger and faster than normal plants
questions.why: Georgina says after adapting, they're stronger and more resilient when they return to Earth.
